evCargoVan.resaleValueAssumption:
Resale Value 
Resale values are modeled from interpolation of California Air Resources Board (CARB) resale values as published in their Advanced Clean Trucks TCO Calculator, May 8th 2019 (section ResTab, A130). While CARB provides specific percentages, here formulas are used that model these percentages as closely as possible and interpolate over vehicle age. Resale value takes into consideration age (years) but not mileage. You can adjust the resale value starting assumption to suit your needs or fit your lender’s own guidance.
Light Duty Vehicle % Resale Value 
The resale value of light duty on road vehicles (weight classes 1-2) is derived using this formula: resale value = ev purchase cost * 0.9429 * EXP(-0.084 * year)
Medium Duty Vehicle % Resale Value
The resale value of medium duty on-road vehicles (weight classes 3 - 6) is derived using this formula: resale value = ev purchase cost * 0.8826 * EXP(-0.1 * year)
Heavy Duty Vehicle %Resale Value
The resale value of heavy-duty on road vehicles (weight classes 7 - 8) is derived using this formula: resale value = ev purchase cost * -0.0003 * year3 + 0.0136 * year2 -0.2057 * year +1.2336

subtitles.nameVal: Airport ZEV and Infrastructure Pilot Program
subtitles.content: The Airport Zero Emissions Vehicle (ZEV) and Infrastructure Pilot Program improves airport air quality and facilitates use of zero emissions technologies at airports. Created in 2012, the program allows airport sponsors to use Airport Improvement Program (AIP) funds to purchase ZEVs and to construct or modify infrastructure needed to use ZEVs.
The project is ineligible for the grant as the organization type is not eligible.

A public-use airport is an airport open to the public that also meets the following criteria: Publicly owned, or Privately owned but designated by FAA as a reliever, or Privately owned but having scheduled service and at least 2,500 annual enplanements. To be eligible for a grant, an airport must be included in the NPIAS. The NPIAS, which is prepared and published every 2 years, identifies public-use airports that are important to public transportation and contribute to the needs of civil aviation, national defense, and the Postal service. For large and medium primary hub airports, the grant covers 75 percent of eligible costs (or 80 percent for noise program implementation). For small primary, reliever, and general aviation airports, the grant covers a range of 90-95 percent of eligible costs, based on statutory requirements. Please contact your local Airports Office for more details. 90 percent of the funded refueling or recharging station capacity is dedicated for on-airport vehicle use. Therefore, only 10 percent of the funded refueling or recharging station capacity can be dedicated to public use. The sponsor must limit the capacity of refueling and recharging stations to the number of project vehicles and their fueling requirements. Sponsors must operate vehicles acquired under the ZEV Pilot Program at the same level of use estimated in the airport sponsor's application. Partial ZEVs or vehicles utilizing "hybrid" technologies are not considered a ZEV and are not eligible under the ZEV Pilot Program. The costs to retrofit the vehicle for a specific airport purpose are not eligible. The airport sponsor must use these useful life assumptions to calculate project emission reduction. Sponsors must; Own or lease all new or retrofitted vehicles and equipment purchased through the ZEV Pilot Program. Not use ZEV Pilot Program funding for tenant-owned vehicles or equipment (e.g., airline vehicles). Not lease ZEV vehicles and equipment purchased under the ZEV Pilot Program to airport tenants. subtitles.content: Evergy rebates reduce the upfront cost of installing publicly accessible Level 2 and DCFC charging stations at your place of business for fleet and public charging.

This project meets the criteria for eligibility and is eligible for $12,500. 5 of the 7.2kW level 2 charger(s) with a purchase cost of $350 qualify for up to $2,500 per port = $12,500 (surplus $10,750). The surplus eligible amounts of $10,750 can be appplied towards the $27,270 instalation costs.

Organizations applying for the program must be non-residential. * Funds available for Rebates are limited.·
* This Rebate is valid for Customers in the Evergy Kansas Central and Evergy Kansas Metro territories on a first come, first-served basis.·
* To be eligible to participate in the Rebate, Customers must be a non-residential customer of Evergy being served under any commercial rate schedule that is not in collections or subject to an active payment agreement.·
* Customers must have the right to install, own, operate, and maintain EVSE on the site, which must be within the previously identified Evergy territories.·
* Customer must agree to install, own, and operate new, qualified EVSE at Highway Corridor, Public, Workplace, Fleet or Multifamily sites and maintain the respective EVSE in good working order at the site at Customer's expense for at least five years after installation.·
* The application must be submitted by the Customer through the Evergy website.·
* Rebates must be claimed within six months of the date of EVSE installation.·
* Sites within 1 mile of a major highway must install at least 2 DCFC units.
